newsitem.title: USA: BEFORE THE BELL - Galileo tumbles.
newsitem.headline: BEFORE THE BELL - Galileo tumbles.

text.p: Shares of Galileo Corp tumbled in pre-opening trading on Thursday after the fiber and electro-optic company said it likely would see a loss in fiscal 1997.
The shares fell 12-3/8 to 6-1/4 before the market opened. The Sturbridge, Mass., company made the forecast for fiscal 1997 late on Wednesday, adding that it had lost Xerox Corp as a major customer.
"That looks like the disaster du jour," a trader said.

Among other shares, USLIFE Corp rose five to 46-3/4 on news of a merger between the company and American General in a stock deal worth $1.8 billion. American General was unchanged after closing on Wednesday at 41-1/2.

Traders reported no trade in Finnish telecommunications equipment maker Nokia Group after the company reported 1996 pre-tax earnings down 21 percent but in line with analysts' forecasts. However, the company's American Depositary Receipts were bid at 65-3/4 with an offer of 66-1/2.
"It'll probably tighten up a little bit," a trader said.

The New York Times' Market Place column wrote that analysts have raised new questions about how costly America Online Inc's business strategy is proving to be. The Internet on-line service last week reported a loss of $155 million in the December quarter.
